explainer: The single best AI-bubble bellwether is the rental price of an installed Nvidia GPU, measured in dollars per GPU-hour, and specifically the H100: it is the daily marginal clearing price for AI compute, it is published by independent indexes (Silicon Data's SDH100RT, SemiAnalysis's one-year contract index), and a CME futures contract on it is pending: the CFTC extended its review to November 9, 2026, so a forward curve is coming but not yet listed. Right now it is saying the opposite of discounting: the Silicon Data index sits at $2.75/hr (Sep 30), a new high, one-year contract rates rose about 40% from $1.70 to $2.35 between October 2025 and March 2026, spot has run at roughly twice contract, and a four-year-old chip is renting for more than it did a year ago while CoreWeave says it has contracted 2020-vintage GPUs out to 2029 at full price. Pair it with three things: neocloud credit spreads (CoreWeave's July loan cleared at SOFR+550 for a 10.44% yield with maintenance covenants, and its CDS implies roughly a coin-flip default probability), which is the financing leg and the one signal already flashing red; server DRAM and HBM contract-price momentum (+13-18% QoQ in 3Q26 after +93-98% in 1Q26, with 4Q26 guided to only +3-8%), because memory is the first physical input that will roll over; and hyperscaler backlog growth versus capex growth (Microsoft commercial RPO +84%, Oracle RPO +363%, roughly $2.4 trillion of committed cloud backlog against about $1 trillion of 2026 capex), because the bubble only deflates if the buyers stop signing. Over the next one to two quarters watch Nvidia's August 26 print for gross margin and customer concentration (three direct customers were already 54% of revenue), the shape of the CME H100/B200 curve if the CFTC clears it in November (a steep backwardation would be the first public forecast of discounting), whether 4Q26 memory contract talks and 2027 HBM4 pricing turn negative, and what ERCOT's December audit says about how much of Texas's 474 GW interconnection queue is phantom demand. The threshold that would flip the call is simple: the H100 index sustained below about $2.00/hr, or spot trading below the one-year contract rate, while Blackwell and Rubin volumes keep arriving; until then compute is being sold at a premium, not a discount, and the risk lives in who is borrowing to build it rather than in the price of the product.

indicators.name: H100 rental price, $/GPU-hour (Silicon Data index; 1-yr contract and spot)
indicators.value: $2.81/hr index (+1.4% 7d) Oct 7, a new high (Oct 2: $2.77); H200 $3.32 (+2.9% 7d); MI300X $2.64 (+0.4%); A100 $1.52 (+3.8%); Nebius H100 list +17% live since Oct 1; CME futures still not listed (CFTC review to Nov 9)
indicators.why: This is the marginal clearing price of installed AI compute and the most direct public read on whether capacity is being discounted; it is published daily, and a CME-listed futures contract on it is pending (CFTC review extended to Nov 9, 2026).
indicators.watch: Bearish flip if the Silicon Data H100 index holds below ~$2.00/hr for a month, if spot trades below the one-year contract rate (inversion), or if the CME H100 curve lists in steep (>15%) backwardation; the Oct-2025 trough of $1.70 is the floor to remember.
indicators.note: Oct 7: Silicon Data's SDH100RT is $2.81 (+1.4% over 7 days), up from $2.77 on Oct 2 and $2.75 on Sep 30, so the run of highs resumed after last week's plateau. H200 is $3.32 (down from $3.37 on Oct 2 but +2.9% on 7 days), MI300X $2.64, A100 $1.52 (down from $1.58 on Oct 2, but +3.8% on 7 days; still above the $1.50 trigger). The page's FAQ box quotes $2.53 for H100, which does not match the $2.81 headline index; the headline is used here. No commentary on the move. The one contract-vs-spot marker on file is Tencent's reported ~$7B five-year lease of ~100,000 Nvidia GPUs from Oracle in Southeast Asia (about $1.60/GPU-hr at full utilisation) against $2.81 on-demand. No CME/Silicon Data futures news this week.

indicators.name: B200 / Blackwell rental price, $/GPU-hour (on-demand)
indicators.value: Silicon Data B200 $5.88 (+0.3% 7d) Oct 7 (Oct 2: $5.86); B300 $6.68 (+1.5% 7d), vs $6.70 Oct 2; B200/H100 ~2.09x; Nebius B200 +19%, B300 +21% live since Oct 1; CoreWeave running Vera Rubin NVL72 in production
indicators.why: Blackwell is where new supply lands, so this is the first place a glut would show; if B200 rates fell toward H100 rates while Rubin ships, capacity would be outrunning demand.
indicators.watch: Bearish if tier-1 neocloud B200 on-demand drops below ~$4.50/hr, if the B200/H100 price ratio compresses below ~2x, or if lead times for 8-GPU Blackwell nodes fall to same-week availability.
indicators.note: Oct 7: the B200 index is $5.88 (+0.3% 7d), essentially flat on Oct 2, and B300 is $6.68. With H100 at $2.81 the B200/H100 ratio is 2.09x, down from 2.12x on Oct 2 purely because H100 rose faster; it is closing on the 2x flip line but B200 is far above the $4.50 trigger. Silicon Data's B200 commentary still says supply is catching up with demand, with large labs locking up multi-year reserved capacity, and that Blackwell's per-GPU throughput justifies the premium over H100. The page's FAQ box shows $5.45, which does not match the $5.88 headline. Rubin is shipping and Blackwell spot has not softened into it. RunPod and Lambda list prices were not rechecked.

indicators.name: Legacy-GPU residual value: used H100 prices, A100/H100 rates and booked useful lives
indicators.value: A100 index $1.52/hr Oct 7 (Oct 2: $1.58), just above the $1.50 trigger; H100 $2.81, H200 $3.32 both up; used H100 SXM ~$18-27K by age vs $30K list (Jun); lenders underwrite GPUs on 3-4 yr schedules vs Nvidia's 'up to a decade' and want >25% residual guarantees; Amazon reportedly putting ~$8B of Grace Blackwell chips in a financing vehicle (~5-yr replacement cycle); MSFT/Meta lives unchanged
indicators.why: Depreciation is the biggest cost in a GPU cloud; if old chips still earn money the 5-6 year accounting lives hold and no write-downs are coming, whereas collapsing used-H100 prices would be the first hard evidence of oversupply.
indicators.watch: Bearish if 8-GPU H100 servers trade below ~50% of new-build cost on the secondary market, if A100/H100 rental rates fall below ~$1.50/hr, or if any hyperscaler extends server lives beyond 6 years to flatter earnings; also watch for Hopper impairments at neoclouds.
indicators.note: Oct 7: the A100 index is $1.52, down from $1.58 on Oct 2 and only 2 cents above the $1.50 bearish trigger, although the page shows +3.8% over 7 days, so the daily prints are noisy rather than a clear break. H100 ($2.81) and H200 ($3.32) are well clear of anything resembling residual stress, so the rental side of residual value is intact for the newer Hopper parts; the oldest part is the one to watch. Lender-side facts are carried from Oct 2 (Reuters survey on 3-4 year underwriting; Amazon's ~$8B Grace Blackwell SPV, aiming for an investment-grade rating). No new used-H100 prints, impairments or useful-life changes found Oct 3-7.

indicators.name: All-in AI data-center build cost, $ per GW (with GPUs / ex-GPUs)
indicators.value: ~$47B/GW Vera Rubin (≈$32B racks + ≈$15B shell/power/cooling); ~$60B/GW gas-powered campus (Orennia); Project Jupiter $165B for 2.45 GW ≈ $67B/GW all-in; TCS Hyderabad $7.4B for 1 GW ex-GPU shell; CDC Gregadoo (Wagga Wagga) A$15B ≈ US$10B for a 'gigawatt-scale' ex-GPU campus, concept phase
indicators.why: Cost per GW sets the revenue a campus must earn per GPU-hour to clear its cost of capital; rising cost means supply is constrained (good for rental prices) but raises the bar for returns and the size of the debt stack.
indicators.watch: Discounting signal if Nvidia rack ASPs or $/GW start falling (Nvidia gross margin guided below ~72%, rack prices cut) while rental $/hr does not rise; bubble-risk signal if ex-GPU cost (power, shell, turbines) keeps inflating faster than rental rates.
indicators.note: No new $/GW datapoint found for Oct 3-7, so the ledger is unchanged: Oracle's Project Jupiter ($165B for 2.45 GW, ~$67B/GW, force majeure Sep 24), the Orennia ~$60B/GW gas-campus benchmark, the ~$47B/GW Vera Rubin figure and CDC's A$15B Gregadoo concept. The cost-of-capital side moved against builders this week instead: the 10-year Treasury hit 5.365% on Oct 7, its highest since April 2002 (inference: a debt-funded campus needs a higher rental yield to clear the same hurdle). Memory input costs keep rising (see memory_prices).

indicators.name: Server DRAM / HBM contract price momentum (QoQ) and DRAM spot
indicators.value: Samsung Q3 prelim (Oct 8): op profit 107.4T won (+20% QoQ, +783% y/y), sales 195T won, HBM4 sales rising steeply ahead of Vera Rubin; DRAMeXchange DDR4 8Gb avg $26 at Q3-end (+23.8% QoQ); spot Oct 7: DDR5 16Gb $58.40 (+0.40%), DDR4 16Gb $83.59 flat; TrendForce 4Q26 (via Goldman): server DRAM +10-15% QoQ, NAND +15-20%; Micron FQ4 GM 87%, FQ1 guide $61.5B; 2027 HBM ASP +121% (TrendForce)
indicators.why: Memory is the tightest physical input to AI servers (HBM is 25-30% of a Rubin rack) and contract prices are negotiated quarterly, so this is the earliest cyclical input to turn; a price rollover would precede GPU discounting.
indicators.watch: Bearish when server DRAM or HBM contract prices go negative QoQ, when 2027 HBM4 contracts are signed at lower prices, or when DRAMeXchange DDR5 spot falls >20% from peak; also watch whether CSPs cut memory per system (Tesla halved AI5 LPDDR5; GPU makers evaluating 8-Hi vs 12-Hi HBM). Near term: SK hynix Q3 around Oct 27-28 (date unconfirmed), Samsung full Q3 results later in October, TrendForce 4Q26 contract settlement, Micron's FQ1 print in December.
indicators.note: Oct 8: Samsung's preliminary Q3 is out (08:28 KST): operating profit 107.4T won, the first quarter above 100T and the fourth straight record, on sales of 195T won. Against consensus it is in line (about 106.1T to 108.7T depending on the survey), so no upside surprise, but also no sign of rollover. Its release says memory shortage and 'chipflation' continued, HBM4 sales jumped ahead of Nvidia's Vera Rubin, and DDR4 8Gb averaged $26 at quarter-end (+23.8% QoQ, over 4x year-on-year), NAND 128Gb MLC $30.61. DRAM spot (TrendForce, Oct 7 18:10 Taipei) is flat at the high: DDR5 16Gb $58.40 (+0.40%), DDR4 16Gb $83.588 (0.00%), DDR4 8Gb $46.357 (+0.08%). TrendForce's Sep 24 4Q26 forecast (as relayed by Goldman) has server DRAM +10-15% QoQ and NAND +15-20%, a firmer 4Q than the +3-8% on file earlier, though long-term agreements cap how far prices can rise. Micron was +4% on Oct 7 (TheStreet).

indicators.name: Power constraint: ERCOT interconnection queue, gas-turbine backlog and lead times
indicators.value: 474 GW ERCOT queue (~90% data centers); Texas TCEQ data-center permit freeze since Sep 21, compliance report due Oct 19; BNEF: 49.8 GW delayed; GE Vernova 116 GW gas backlog + slot reservations (Q2; target >=125 GW by year-end), ~20 GW/yr output; Oracle force majeure on 2.45 GW Project Jupiter; Senate blocked Ratepayer Protection Act 57-43 (Sep 30); Dover DE and Dixon CA moratoria
indicators.why: Power, not chips, is now the binding constraint on new capacity, which keeps installed GPUs scarce and rental prices firm; it also reveals how much announced demand is speculative once regulators force projects to prove financing.
indicators.watch: ERCOT files its Batch Zero eligibility-verification and community-impact reports by Dec 10, 2026 for the Dec 17 PUCT open meeting: large queue withdrawals (BNEF flags 49.8 GW at risk) would show phantom demand. Turbine slot cancellations or resales, falling data-center PPA prices, or turbine prices retreating from the $600/kW 2027 forecast would signal the build is slowing. Nearer: TCEQ compliance report Oct 19, GE Vernova Q3 webcast Oct 28, Project Jupiter air-permit decision Nov 23.
indicators.note: No new queue, turbine or permit numbers surfaced for Oct 3-7; the Texas pause stands. Abbott's Sep 21 directive tells TCEQ to suspend action on all data-center permits until ERCOT finishes its queue audit, with a compliance report due Oct 19 that is a reporting deadline, not an expiry. Critics (Public Citizen) call it vague; the scope for island-mode generation is unclear. Fort Worth has a 90-day pause on new data-center developments. GE Vernova's Q3 webcast is listed for Oct 28 (07:30 EDT), the next hard read on whether slot reservations (63 GW at Q2, firm backlog 53 GW) are converting. Prior items unchanged: Oracle's Sep 24 force majeure on Project Jupiter, the Senate vote on who pays for grid build-out, and Exelon's ~40% cut to high-probability data-center load.

indicators.name: Hyperscaler capex vs cloud backlog (RPO) growth, and capex as % of cloud revenue
indicators.value: Anthropic prospectus: $518B of compute commitments over 7-10 yrs, ~80% non-cancelable; Anthropic pre-IPO investor session Oct 14, formal marketing week of Nov 9; Amazon ~$220B 2026 capex plus a reported $8B off-balance-sheet chip vehicle; Oracle RPO $664B but force majeure on Project Jupiter; Micron ~$150B RPO; Marvell lifted FY28 revenue to ~$20B and set a $70-90B FY31 target (Oct 6); Goldman: US hyperscaler capex $1.4T in 2027
indicators.why: Capex is the supply side and RPO is the contracted demand side; as long as backlog grows faster than capex the build is pre-sold, but capex above 100% of cloud revenue with negative free cash flow means the cycle is now funded by debt and equity and is sensitive to any demand wobble.
indicators.watch: Bearish if RPO growth decelerates below capex growth for two quarters, if 2027 capex consensus (+57% per Morgan Stanley) gets cut or 'digestion' language appears, or if backlog concentration in a few AI labs (OpenAI, Anthropic) produces a cancellation or renegotiation; Oracle's Project Jupiter force majeure is the first payment-deferral mechanism triggered on a Stargate site - watch whether it spreads.
indicators.note: Oct 6-7 adds a supplier-side read rather than a buyer-side one. Marvell's investor day (Oct 6) raised FY28 revenue to about $20B (about $18B data center), pulled its $18B data-center target forward almost a year, set a FY31 range of $70-90B against ~$47B consensus, and sized the addressable market at ~$400B by 2030; custom compute FY29 is now above $12B. That is the vendor view that the build keeps compounding; shares rose on the day and slipped pre-market Oct 7. Buyer side is unchanged since Oct 2: Anthropic's Oct 14 session is still on, with the $518B commitment stack and ~$60B Broadcom-led chip financing; Amazon's $8B SPV is still reported as under exploration. A 10-year yield at 5.3%+ raises the carrying cost of all of this (inference, not in a source). Next hard data: TSMC Oct 15 (guide $44.6-45.8B), then late-October hyperscaler prints.

indicators.name: Neocloud financing: CoreWeave loan/bond spreads, CDS, vendor backstops, customer concentration
indicators.value: CoreWeave debt ~$35.6B, trailing net leverage ~6.8x, EBITDA interest cover 2.7x, backlog $103.7B, 2031 unsecured bond yield 'low teens' vs 9.75% at April issue (Seeking Alpha via Pluang, Oct 1); CRWV $87.39 (-2.5%) at Oct 5 close, 52-wk $60.55-153.20; Broadcom-led ~$60B chip financing ($42B senior + $18B junior led by Blackstone), pricing undisclosed; Amazon ~$8B chip SPV, IG rating the aim; lenders want >25% residual guarantees
indicators.why: Neoclouds are the levered marginal builder of GPU capacity; their cost of debt, covenants and dependence on Nvidia backstops show whether lenders still believe rental prices will cover depreciation, and they are the first place a compute-price decline turns into forced selling.
indicators.watch: Escalation if new deals price above SOFR+600 or 11% yields, CDS above 1,000bp, deals pulled or downsized, Nvidia's rent-back backstop extended to tier-1 neoclouds, or a top customer (CoreWeave's A/B/C are 36%/26%/10% of revenue) renegotiates; improvement if spreads retrace toward the April 9.75% level or if CoreWeave can tap convertible/equity-linked money on Nebius-like terms.
indicators.note: No new CoreWeave debt print or Broadcom/Amazon pricing surfaced Oct 3-7. The one new number is a yield: a Seeking Alpha note relayed by Pluang (Oct 1) puts CoreWeave's 2031 unsecured bond in the low teens, against the 9.75% coupon it priced in April. If right that is through the 11% escalation line in the watch field, but it is a single secondary source with no quoted price, so the signal is held at neutral until a bond quote or loan print confirms it. The same note calls liquidity adequate: $103.7B backlog, 2.7x interest cover, 2026 capex guided at $30-35B. Equity is soft: CRWV closed $87.39 on Oct 5, about 43% below its $153.20 high, while the rest of the AI complex hit records on Oct 6. Financing remains available at very large size but in tranches that price in downside (junior Blackstone piece, residual guarantees).

indicators.name: Nvidia data-center revenue growth, gross margin and customer concentration
indicators.value: DC rev $89.0B +117% YoY (Q2 FY27), GM 75.0%, Q3 guide $108B at 74%; one direct customer >=10% (16%); supply commitments $279B; $150B buyback added Sep 28; NVDA $237.47 (-0.7%) Oct 7, below its record; Samsung says HBM4 sales jumped ahead of Vera Rubin (Oct 8); $500B chip-collateral plan facing lender pushback; Q3 FY27 report ~Nov, GTC Washington Nov 30-Dec 3
indicators.why: Nvidia's margin is the purest read on whether GPUs are being discounted at the source, and its concentration plus growing vendor-financing (backstops, campus guarantees) shows how much of demand is circular.
indicators.watch: Bearish if gross margin is guided below ~72% for more than one quarter, data-center revenue grows <5% sequentially, three-customer concentration exceeds 60% in the 10-Q, DSO climbs past 60 days, or backstop commitments expand beyond the $108.5B disclosed; Q3 FY27 report due ~Nov 2026.
indicators.note: Operating figures are unchanged from the Aug 26 10-Q and the Sep 28 buyback; there is no Nvidia print before November. Read-throughs this week are volume-positive: Samsung (Oct 8) reports steeply higher HBM4 sales ahead of Vera Rubin and a 107.4T won quarter, and Marvell (Oct 6) lifted its custom-silicon and interconnect targets, which is a reminder that a growing share of AI spend goes to custom ASICs rather than Nvidia (headline reports Google ties $120B of chip purchases to Marvell equity warrants; not verified beyond the headline). NVDA slipped 0.7% to $237.47 on Oct 7 after the S&P 500 and Nasdaq set records Oct 6. Financing remains the soft spot: lenders still resist Nvidia's $500B collateralised plan (3-4 year underwriting, >25% residual guarantees). No public forward curve for GPU rentals (CFTC review to Nov 9). Nvidia's GTC Washington is Nov 30-Dec 3, not October as in 2025.
